sections.title: One of Hungarian's busiest prefixes
sections.content: el- is one of the hardest-working igekötők in Hungarian — it glues onto many different verbs, usually to mark that an action is getting under way or moving off. Attach it to kezd ('start') and you get elkezd, 'to start, to begin (doing something)'; attach it to indul ('set off') and you get elindul, 'to set off, to depart'. Back in Unit 21 you met kezdődik for a schedule item starting on its own (A munkaidőm kilenckor kezdődik); elkezd is the personal version — the one where you are the one starting something.

items.english: In the morning at eight I set off from home.

items.spanish: Károly és Gábor együtt elindulnak a boltba.
items.english: Károly and Gábor set off to the shop together.

sections.content: elkezd almost always pairs with a bare infinitive, just like the kezd dolgozni pattern you already know — elkezdek dolgozni, elkezdesz olvasni. elindul, on the other hand, behaves exactly like the plain indul you already met with buses and trains, just with a stronger sense of 'right, I'm off' — and it takes the same -ból/-ből or -ról/-ről 'starting point' case.
